title: One Word Made Flesh
english: …this same one, as God, stripped death of its spoils. Again, the soldiers kept guard over him as one dead, and the gatekeepers of Hades, beholding him as God, cowered (Job 38:17).

You will say that this one and that one are the same, not one and another, nor one in another, nor one through another. For the Word made flesh, being one, brought these things and those together into one, as he willed, in a manner beyond telling. He gave his flesh to serve the sufferings, and he made use of his Godhead for the signs and wonders; but as it is not right for the Word to be separated from the flesh, so the sufferings must be interwoven with the wonders. For he who went down into Hades as one dead, this same one as God set the dead free. Otherwise, how do angels minister at a tomb, how do they appear in white to the women, as for a bridegroom, and how did they say to them, 'You are looking for Jesus…'
translator_notes: The section opens in mid-sentence; its first word, ἄνθρωπος, is rendered at the end of the previous section ('as a man…').
πυλωροὶ τοῦ ᾅδου ... ἔπτηξαν echoes Job 38:17 LXX (πυλωροὶ δὲ ᾅδου ἰδόντες σε ἔπτηξαν).
ἀρρήτῳ λόγῳ: 'in a manner beyond telling'; Hesychius plays on Λόγος, the Word, and λόγῳ, 'telling'.
ἐπεί πως ... πὼς δὲ ... πὼς δὲ: read as ἐπεὶ πῶς, 'otherwise, how...?', the argument that only God's presence explains the angels at the tomb.
The angels' words run on into the next section; the quotation is split there with an ellipsis.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia ii in sanctum pascha (Khazarzar) u01 rem early

title: The Angel and the Prophets
english: '…the Nazarene, who was crucified. He is not here, for he has risen, as he said (Mark 16:6; Matthew 28:6). That is, heaven is his place; send the myrrh there. He has risen; it was not we who raised him. For your sake we rolled away the stone, for before we came down the tomb had already been emptied. He has risen, as he himself said.'

What the angel said not even a prophet could explain. Hosea tells the time of the resurrection; Isaiah knows it, but how it will be he does not understand. For these are the words of Hosea's prophecy: 'Come, let us go and return to the Lord our God, for he has struck us, and he will heal us; he will strike, and he will bind us up after two days; on the third day we shall rise and live before him' (Hosea 6:1–2). Hear again what Isaiah sounded on the trumpet: 'Lebanon has been put to shame; Sharon has become marshland…' (Isaiah 33:9)
translator_notes: The section opens inside the angels' words begun in the previous section ('You are looking for Jesus…'). The first sentence blends Mark 16:6 (Ἰησοῦν ζητεῖτε τὸν Ναζαρηνὸν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον) and Matthew 28:6 (οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε· ἠγέρθη γὰρ καθὼς εἶπεν); the rest of the speech is Hesychius' own expansion and is not cited.
Hosea 6:1–2: Hesychius reads πέπαικεν ('has struck') for the Septuagint's ἥρπακεν (the edition sets the word outside the quotation marks) and leaves out ὑγιάσει; the English follows his wording.
Isaiah 33:9a follows the Septuagint (ᾐσχύνθη 'put to shame', ἕλη 'marshes'), not the Hebrew 'withers ... like a desert'. The quotation continues in the next section.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia ii in sanctum pascha (Khazarzar) u01 rem mid

title: Now I Will Arise
english: '…Galilee and Carmel will be laid bare. Now I will arise,' says the Lord, 'now I will be glorified, now I will be lifted up. Now you will see, now you will be put to shame' (Isaiah 33:9–11).

For he was directing these words at the Jews: "Now I will arise, when I raise up Adam, whom the transgression cast down. Now I will be glorified, when I establish for the nations freedom from the passions. Now I will be lifted up, when I lift your firstfruits into the heavens and raise to the throne of the cherubim 'the form of the servant' (Philippians 2:7) that I have taken from you. Now you will see the types coming to an end and the truth in flower. Now you will be put to shame, you who slander with words and are defeated by the facts."
For glory belongs to God, to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: The section opens in the middle of the quotation of Isaiah 33:9–11, which begins at the end of the previous section ('Lebanon has been put to shame; Sharon has become marshland'); the citation stands at the close of the quoted verses.
φανερὰ ἔσται: Septuagint 'will be manifest, exposed'; rendered 'will be laid bare'.

Πρὸς … τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τὸν λόγον ἀπετείνετο: 'he was directing these words at the Jews'. The following clauses are the Lord's own first-person voice, expounding each 'now' of the verse, so they are set in double quotation marks; the doxology after ὅτι is the preacher's close and stands outside them.

τοῖς ἔθνεσιν τῶν παθῶν συστήσω τὴν ἀπάθειαν: ἀπάθεια with a genitive of what one is free from, 'freedom from the passions'. Hesychius plays on παθῶν / ἀπάθειαν; τῶν παθῶν could also be read as 'through (my) sufferings', giving 'when through my sufferings I establish freedom from suffering for the nations'. The plainer construction is kept and the alternative noted here.

τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀπαρχήν: 'your firstfruits', the human nature Christ took 'from you' (ἐξ ὑμῶν), that is, from Israel; it is the same as 'the form of the servant' in the next phrase. A link with 1 Corinthians 15:20 (ἀπαρχή) is possible but the wording is not close enough to cite inline.

εἰς τὴν καθέδραν τῶν χερουβίν: 'to the throne of the cherubim', the seat of God above the cherubim. It may recall Psalm 79:2 LXX (Psalm 80:1, ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῶν χερουβίν), but the wording differs, so it is not cited inline.
παυομένους τοὺς τύπους, ἀνθοῦσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν: the Old Testament types ceasing and the truth they foreshadowed 'in flower'.
συκοφαντοῦντες ῥήμασιν καὶ ἡττώμενοι πράγμασιν: the contrast is words against deeds; πράγμασιν rendered 'the facts', the events of the Resurrection that refute the slander.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia ii in sanctum pascha (Khazarzar) u01 rem close
